To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the activation of lysosomal enzymes is stimulus specific and the events related to their elaboration in vivo are subject of modulation.

the macrophage lysosome is an important organelle for the expression of the macrophage functional phenotype and that the activation profile of macrophage lysosomes is stimulus specific and is subject to modulation.
the macrophage elicited by three different stimulants (TG, PP, and LPS) have different levels of lysosomal enzyme activities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the molecular and genetic events that underlie the activation of the macrophage lysosomes.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of the macrophage lysosomes in the context of their role in the inflammatory response.
the study of the activation profile of lysosomal hydrolases in rat macrophages in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the activation of macrophage lysosome is a stimulus specific phenomenon and is not a general phenomenon.
the three stimulans, though eliciting macrophages at different levels, have a similar modulating effect on their lysosomal enzyme activities.
the macrophages eliciting agents (TG, PP, and LPS) induce the macrophage to undergo a progressive activation of lysosomal enzymes, which may be correlated to the progressive maturation of the cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the macrophages activated by LPS are less active in the elaboration of lysosomal enzymes compared to the cells activated by the other two stimulants.
the macrophages elicitable from the rat peritoneum in response to TG, PP and LPS are different in nature, and the events related to their activation are stimulus specific.
, the macrophages elicitable in response to the various stimulants are not identical in their nature and behaviour and that their functional properties are also different.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the activation profile of the macrophage lysosome is stimulus specific and the activation of the lysosomal enzymes in macrophages eliciting in response to LLS is different from that in the TG and the PP elicited macrohages.
the activation of lysosomal enzymes can be a useful marker to assess the in vivo status of the macrophages.
macrophage activation in response to the different stimuli can be assessed by measuring the activities of these lysosomal enzymes.
